highlights.title: Revolut outage hits 'multiple services' as thousands of users report app issues
highlights.summary: Some users of the British neobank reported being unable to make some payments or access funds in its app on Tuesday.
body: Revolut has been by an outage which it says is impacting "multiple services", as thousands of customers report problems.
Users of the British bank have flagged being unable to make some payments or access funds via its app on Tuesday morning.
Platform outage monitor Downdetector had seen more than 1,500 user reports of issues with Revolut services shortly after 08:00 BST.
"We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services," a Revolut spokesperson told the BBC - adding "we can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe."

highlights.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
highlights.summary: The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade while renewable energy growth slows down, a new report shows. Electricity demand is also climbing faster than it has in more than a decade with more data centers, factories, and electric vehicles plugging into the grid.
body: Data centers are demanding more energy, and the Trump administration is making sure fossil fuels meet the moment.

America’s energy landscape is already shifting as a result, according to the report published last week by the nonprofit Environmental Defense Fund and research firm Atlas Public Policy. If all the gas projects in the development pipeline complete construction, they could lock in more pollution and higher electricity prices for decades, the authors warn.
“The U.S. power sector is at a new inflection point, with decisions made today shaping the cost, reliability, and emissions profile of the grid for decades to come,” the report says.

While the US still generates 60 percent of its electricity from fossil fuels, renewables have quickly gained ground. Wind and solar produced more electricity together than coal for the first time in 2024. Solar was the fastest-growing source of new electricity generation that year, accounting for 81 percent of added capacity. Globally, solar has become the cheapest power source in most of the world.

highlights.title: Boulter puts rain delays behind her to progress at Japan Open
highlights.summary: A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume.
body: The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals.

The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round).

On Monday, the match between Boulter and Sakatsume had barely started when the players were forced off court after torrential rain arrived in Osaka. Given the venue didn't have a roof, the court was open to all of the elements.
By that point, only three games had been played in the first set, with Sakatsume leading 2-1 at the time of the suspension.

highlights.title: "This act is intended to demonstrate solidarity with Palestine" - Umurangi Generation studio blocks new game Penguin Colony from being sold in Israel
highlights.summary: Origame Digital, the studio behind 2020's critically acclaimed Umurangi Generation, has just released a new game but banned it from being sold in Israel.
body: Penguin Colony is a Lovecraftian horror game experienced through the eyes of a penguin, based on author H.P. Lovecraft's story At the Mountains of Madness. Fellow Traveller, the game's publisher, confirmed that Penguin Colony is not on sale in Israel in a Steam community thread. The thread was created by a Steam user living in Israel wondering if the game had been delisted from Steam.

"While in general we seek to bring our games to as many potential players as possible, we believe strongly that developers have the right to control where their games are sold," Fellow Traveller replied. "In this case, the developer asked us to block sale in Israel. In the absence of more organised sanctions, this act is intended to demonstrate solidarity with Palestine. We fully support their decision."

That message is further reinforced by Penguin Colony itself, which features a post-credits scene that makes clear the studio's stance on Israel's genocide of the Palenstinan people. As shared online, the message reads: "The cowardice of the Games Industry during the ongoing genocide of Palestine by Isreal will be recorded by the art it makes."

highlights.title: ‘Big Boys Don’t Cry’ Director Muhammad Mustapha Talks Masculinity Ahead of El Gouna Premiere: ‘The Only Emotion Men Are Allowed to Express Is Anger’
highlights.summary: Egyptian filmmaker Muhammad Mustapha’s “Big Boys Don’t Cry” follows a group of Cairo bodybuilders and nightclub bouncers, offering a view into how men understand and perform masculinity.
body: Mustapha distinguishes that curiosity from a desire to investigate something he saw as inherently wrong. When he began the project in 2016, he approached it as an anthropological and sociological study of masculinity and how it is expressed in different contexts.

His own upbringing gave him a point of reference. Mustapha grew up in what he describes as a “local” Cairo neighborhood, where he was surrounded by its masculine codes. As a studious “nerd,” he could be seen as less masculine there. But when he entered dental school, the same behavior could instead make him appear loud or vulgar.
That contrast helped him recognize how masculinity could shift according to context, a fact he also saw among the men he was observing.
“How they perform their masculinity on stage is different than in front of the pub, is different than when he is addressing a problem, different than when he is with his family,” he says.

highlights.title: ‘How green are our valleys?’: in the footsteps of miners on south Wales’s new forest trail
highlights.summary: The first stage of an ambitious new hiking route that will link woodlands across Wales takes walkers into the wild hills above the valleys’ old mining villages. Bracken and heather ripple across the plateau.
body: I’m hiking the new Llwybr Coedwig Cymru Trail, or Wales Forest Trail. Running from Porthkerry Park, near Barry, to Pont Walby, close to Glynneath, this 50-mile (80km) pilot route is the first section of what the National Forest for Wales hopes will eventually be a trail linking woodlands across the length and breadth of Wales: a sylvan counterpart to the Wales Coast Path.

My father grew up in one of the valleys’ mining villages and, when I visited relatives there as a child, the disconnection of those post-industrial communities from the wild hills that loomed above them was striking. Mountain bikers have long discovered the region’s potential, but walkers still tend to head for the more obvious trails that wind through the national parks or along the coast. This pilot trail seems a good excuse to explore untapped footpaths.

With the sea behind me, I set off from the oak leaf sculpture that marks the trail’s start. The viaduct ahead once carried coal to Barry docks, but today it stands over Caffe Matteo, busy with dog walkers sipping cappuccinos. Leaving them behind, I cross the park between the soft greens of birch and oak trees.

highlights.title: Googlebook review: Google’s new laptops are woefully underbaked
highlights.summary: Great hardware let down by software flaws on these pricey machines that combine ChromeOS with Android. Google’s attempt to create a new type of laptop to compete with Windows and macOS machines is finally here, combining the best of ChromeOS and Android into the new Googlebook.
body: For years, Chromebooks have been the boss of budget laptops, but Googlebooks take a different, far more premium approach. Made by a range of traditional PC makers, including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, they start at £999 (€1,099/ $899 / A$2,299 ) – a far cry from the £160 Chromebooks.

While Google does not make these machines directly, it has set strict hardware quality standards that the laptops must reach. That includes backlit keyboards, haptic trackpads, fingerprint readers, crisp touchscreens, decent speakers and modern fast chips with at least 16GB of RAM.
It is a list of specs you should expect with a premium Windows PC, but those start at a much higher price, primarily thanks to RAMageddon.
As such, the Acer Googlebook 14 and the Asus Googlebook 14 I’ve been testing have excellent hardware with satisfying keyboards, great trackpads and quality screens.

highlights.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
highlights.summary: CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition - when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they'd get from government bonds.
body: Now, I have also asked if the AI industry is a bubble, but when the SPAC King echoes concerns held by a lady whose ongoing question about AI is “ How are we planning on affording this, champs? ”, that’s a very different signal. When I say “yikes,” it’s one thing. When Elon Musk says it, that’s something else.

To make things worse for CoreWeave, Brannin McBee, one of the company’s cofounders, told the Financial Times — also last week, on the same day as Palihapitiya’s post — that the company wants to have its debt be investment-grade, rather than junk, so that it can borrow from insurers, as their capital is, in his words, “unlimited.” This is not entirely unreasonable — earlier this year, CoreWeave secured its first investment-grade chip loan. But when you talk about wanting to tap into the enormous sums of money that insurers have, that’s the kind of thing that makes investors afraid that CoreWeave — already a massive debtor — is going to borrow even more.

highlights.title: England unchanged for World Cup clash vs France with Lewis absent again
highlights.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France.
body: AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga.
Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis.
As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.
Last weekend against Tonga, Welsby and Warrington Wolves winger Matty Ashton were the unused substitutes - with Wigan Warriors speedster Zach Eckersley getting the nod instead.

highlights.title: 5 Best Halloween 'Peanuts' Comics That Don't Involve the Great Pumpkin
highlights.summary: Halloween in Charles Schulz's Peanuts frequently meant it was time for another run at the Great Pumpkin. This running gag, introduced in 1959, was sort of like Schulz's answer to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot.
body: The roots of the Great Pumpkin joke seem to lie in a comic strip from Oct. 23, 1959. Charlie Brown complains to Patty that he couldn't get a Halloween mask from the store... because they'd already moved on to selling all their Christmas decorations.

It's interesting to see this complaint in a comic strip from 67 years ago. We often assume that the aggressive commercialization of Christmas in particular has gotten worse in the 21st century, but it turns out it was still an issue when our grandparents were young.

It also helps bring the Great Pumpkin into context as a parody of that commercialization. As time went on and Schulz evolved the joke, the Great Pumpkin picked up enough of its own unique lore that it moved away from its origins. In its first appearance, it's more obviously a case of a little kid getting Halloween and Christmas confused courtesy of consumerism. By the '70s, it had become more of a commentary on religious culture and blind faith, with Linus occasionally going so far as to proselytize door-to-door on the Great Pumpkin’s behalf.

highlights.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
highlights.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

highlights.title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for lamb meatballs with spinach and chickpea stew, and red rice
highlights.summary: Serve this warm and juicy meatball sabanekh with Iraqi tomato rice for a comforting meal that’s made to be shared. This is the kind of meal I love for its generosity and simplicity.
body: Sabanekh is a beloved spinach stew across the Levant, and here I’ve added lamb meatballs to make it a more substantial meal. The combination of cumin, coriander and garlic gives warmth and depth, while a generous squeeze of lemon brightens everything. Serve with rice or warm flatbread to soak up the delicious, fragrant sauce.

Put the mince in a medium bowl, add a teaspoon of salt, half a teaspoon of baharat and a third of a teaspoon of black pepper, and mix well. Shape the meat into 25 balls (about 20g each) and set aside.

Heat two tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan on a medium heat. Add the pine nuts and cook, stirring constantly, for three to four minutes, until golden brown. Spoon the pine nuts into a bowl.

highlights.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
highlights.summary: Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
body: The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.

The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.

The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft — two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant — separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.

highlights.title: OpenAI Engineer Accused of Spying on Executives Ordered to Remain in Custody
highlights.summary: A judge ordered Abdulrahman Alfozan to remain in custody, likening the Saudi government’s offer to secure the former OpenAI engineer’s release to a “blank check.”
body: The former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging a company conference room must stay in custody while he awaits trial, a federal judge ruled on Monday after expressing concerns about his ties to Saudi Arabia.

US prosecutors alleged Abdulrahman Alfozan is a flight risk because the Saudi Arabian government has offered to support him with no strings attached. They cited, for example, the Saudi consulate’s offer to work with a bail bonds firm to help fund Alfozan’s release.

Federal magistrate judge Alex Tse questioned whether Alfozan is an “asset” for the kingdom and how a bond backed by the government could keep him in the country. “I find that problematic,” Tse said. “It seems like a blank check. ‘We’re going to pay whatever the court wants to get him out.’ I’m more interested in people from his family wanting to put up assets.”

William Pernik, an attorney for Alfozan, dismissed the flight risk worries as baseless. But he failed to convince the judge that Alfozan was committed to his life in the US. “There is a real threat here that once he leaves the case is over,” Tse said.

highlights.title: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals
highlights.summary: Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.
body: In front of the Valkyries' raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice - and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too.
"For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said.

"Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do. So I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark and did whatever I could to get the win, and I think I did that tonight."

Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, Allisha Gray added 18 points, and Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise's first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips - 0-10 overall.

highlights.title: Save $40 Off Microsoft's Professional-Grade Xbox Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller
highlights.summary: Do you prefer PlayStation or Xbox controllers? I'm in the latter camp. My favorite PC controllers have always been modeled after Xbox's tried and true asymmetrical layout. And when it comes to Xbox controllers, you can't get much better than the highest end model from Microsoft itself.
body: The Elite Series 2 Core is the official premium controller for Xbox. The Core model is physically identical to the previous generation $200 Xbox Elite Series 2 controller, with integrated pro gaming features like adjustable-tension thumbsticks, wrap-around rubberized grip, and shorter hair trigger locks. The only difference is that the original Elite controller comes with more accessories: extra sets of paddles, thumbsticks, D-pad, and a travel case. The Elite Series 2 Core doesn't come with any of those accessories. You can buy them separately as a component pack for $59.99.

IGN's Jacqueline Thomas reported on rumored leaks that the Elite Series 3 release might be on the horizon. I'm not very optimistic, however, that the launch price will be the same as the Xbox Series 2 controller when it first released at $179.99. Given that the price of the Elite Series 2 with component pack is $200, I expect the same price or higher.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

highlights.title: Don’t be fooled. The AI that was supposed to save us time is doing just the opposite | Gaby Hinsliff
highlights.summary: The government says it can transform the state with AI, but it is no match for the resulting stream of machine-generated slop. And we all pay the cost. Another morning, another avalanche of emails.
body: In theory, email was supposed to save hours of meetings, phone calls and standing over photocopiers. Instead, we just spend hours deleting stuff people wouldn’t have bothered telling us if it had meant picking up the phone, but which they can now spam to their entire database at the click of a button. The glorious ease and convenience of being able to reach the world in seconds came, we now know, with the inconvenience of them being able to reach you right back.

And therein lies the challenge to the government’s hopes of AI helping to transform the machinery of the state on the cheap, saving not only time but billions of pounds in public money. It’s early days, but AI seems not so much to be streamlining public service delivery as gumming it up – partly because, as was once the case with email, the public is using it right back at them.

Whitehall special advisers complain of departments drowning in AI-generated freedom of information requests, an abuse of a system originally intended to empower individuals. MPs’ offices are similarly swamped by AI-generated letters, all of which need to be read by humans for fear of missing something important from a constituent.
points: The government says it can transform the state with AI, but it is no match for the resulting stream of machine-generated slop.
In theory, email was supposed to save hours of meetings, phone calls and standing over photocopiers.

highlights.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people.
body: But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.

The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.

Such changes are coming because agents really do mark a third category of web visitor. They’re not humans, of course, and they use the internet at machine speed. But they’re not quite bots, either, because they’re acting on behalf of individual people to do tasks that can be perfectly legitimate and useful. They just work faster than a person would.

highlights.title: 3 Video Games Where Your Choices Actually Make a Difference
highlights.summary: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when…
body: Large-scale narrative branches are engaging for a reason. They're satisfying, and they make you feel a sense of influence over events and characters you care about. Like with video game romance, however, they have become somewhat stale and predictable in form. So for this list, I decided to look at three games that use branching narratives in bolder and unexpected ways.

Zero Parades: For Dead Spies is the rare piece of interactive media where your choices matter not just for how they influence the story, but for how they shape your actions, too. Hershel, the protagonist of the piece, is a spy. Or, was a spy. A series of catastrophic incidents happened, and she finds herself decommissioned, in a room with a comatose person, and without any idea how she got here. There's a very dangerous game afoot in the fictional town of Portofiro, Zero Parades ' setting, and your job is figuring it out and possibly even finding redemption. Maybe. If you can manage it.

body: Pocket-sized Hong Kong packs more of a punch than its 430-square-mile size might suggest. Split into three main areas—Hong Kong Island, the Kowloon Peninsula, and the New Territories—made up of 18 districts, each with their own rich history, culture, architecture, and foods, there's more than enough to keep the average tourist busy for months, never mind the usual weekend trip.

With more than seven million people packed into over 9,000 high-rises, efficiency is key here, and people will judge you for holding up lines, hesitating with your Octopus card, or lingering over your dim sum table while others are waiting. That said, Hong Kong people are generally kind and helpful when it comes to asking for directions. Most also speak English, which is one of the city’s official languages.
These are the unwritten rules of traveling to Hong Kong you should bookmark to seamlessly go with the flow on your next trip.

highlights.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
highlights.summary: A model developed by researchers at MIT and Boston Children's Hospital adjusts scans on the fly to track fetal movement, potentially sparing families repeat hospital visits.
body: Despite millions of years of evolution, the development of the human fetus remains a complex process that is vulnerable to genetic, environmental, and metabolic disruptions. These disruptions could result in developmental abnormalities, starting with one of the first organs to begin developing in the fetus that continues to develop after birth: the brain.

In a routine prenatal ultrasound, the sonographer will flag possible brain abnormalities for additional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). But imperfect imaging can result in missed or incorrect diagnoses.

To assist with the early detection and treatment of these abnormalities, researchers at MIT, Boston Children’s Hospital, and Inria have developed and trained a deep learning model called E(3)-Pose that helps image the fetus’s head while it’s in motion to capture a high-resolution image that the radiologist can examine. A paper about the work was presented at the 2026 European Conference on Computer Vision.
